chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Amr ibn Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, exalted and mighty, when he meets Him, like an idol-worshipper.'

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: Habitual drinker / one who frequently consumes

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the theological gravity of habitual intoxication by equating the drinker’s spiritual state to that of a polytheist (*mushrik*) at the time of divine encounter. This comparison underscores that while the physical act differs, the internal state of heedlessness and deviation from monotheism renders the drinker spiritually akin to an idol-worshipper. It serves as a critical ethical benchmark in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the severity of *khamr* beyond mere ritual impurity.
